title: Nested Schema Validator with Path-Keyed Errors
prompt: Write a tiny JSON-schema-style validator for form and API payloads. `validate(schema, value)` returns an object mapping each failing path to one message, or `{}` when the value is valid. The root path is `"$"`, object children are `"<path>.<key>"`, array items are `"<path>[<index>]"`. Rules, checked in this order, first failure wins per path: **string** - `"expected string"`, `minLength` -> `"must be at least N characters"`, `maxLength` -> `"must be at most N characters"`, `enum` -> `"must be one of: a, b"`. **number** (finite) - `"expected number"`, `integer` -> `"expected integer"`, `min` -> `"must be >= N"`, `max` -> `"must be <= N"`. **boolean** - `"expected boolean"`. **array** - `"expected array"` (stop), `minItems` -> `"must have at least N items"` at the array's path, and every item is still validated. **object** (non-null, not an array) - `"expected object"` (stop); then for each key of `properties` in schema order: a missing (absent) key gets `"is required"` at the child path if it is in `required`, otherwise it is skipped; present keys (including `null`) are validated. With `additionalProperties: false`, each extra key in the value gets `"is not allowed"`, after the declared properties. Errors appear in traversal order.

explanation.beginner: Write one recursive helper `check(schema, value, path, errors)`. It looks at `schema.type` and handles one level: for a string it checks the type and the length rules one after another and writes only the first failure into `errors[path]`. For an array it checks that the value is an array, then calls itself for every item with the path `path[i]`. For an object it goes through the schema's properties: if the key is missing it only complains when the key is required; otherwise it calls itself with `path.key`. Start the whole thing with path `$`. Because every call writes into the same errors object, the paths line up exactly with where the problem is, which is what a form needs to show the message next to the right input.
explanation.junior: Model the schema as a discriminated union on `type` so each `case` narrows to the right options (a `minItems` on a string schema is a compile error). Use early `return` after a type mismatch: descending into a value of the wrong type would produce noise errors. Distinguish absent from null: `null` is a present value and should fail with `expected string`, which is what users of real validators (Zod, Ajv) expect. Use `hasOwnProperty` for presence so a key named `toString` is not treated as present via the prototype. Array `minItems` is a container-level error; keep validating the items because their paths differ. Complexity is O(n) in the size of the value. Real libraries add unions, refinements, and coercion, but the path-keyed error map is the same shape Zod's `flatten()` or a form library's `errors` object gives you.
